input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date.
input.rationale: Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "early termination", "termination fee", "shortfall" and "minimum" return no provision requiring Customer to pay liquidated damages, a penalty, or a minimum/early-termination charge. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties). On the contrary, § 9.4 lets Customer terminate for convenience owing only Fees for conforming Services delivered, with refund of prepaid Fees; § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges; and § 27.3 allows force-majeure termination "without penalty". The § 2.1 take-or-pay commitment is a volume commitment rather than a liquidated-damages or penalty mechanic and is assessed under the minimum-commitment rule, so it is not flagged here to avoid double-counting the same commercial term.
